A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FaceXFormer by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial scientific and presentation revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original FaceXFormer benchmark results, task-synergy and backbone experiments, bias analysis, and cross-dataset evaluations, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 reports original results across nine facial tasks, revised benchmark comparisons, backbone experiments, and new component ablations in Appendix C.

M1.justification: v2 adds expression-recognition tokens, a classification head, and a loss term. Landmark prediction changes from a regression MLP with Wing loss and one task token to an hourglass network with STAR loss and 68 tokens. Head-pose prediction changes to nine tokens representing a rotation matrix, and age training changes from cross-entropy to combined L1 and cross-entropy loss. The encoder, fusion module, and attention decoder remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds expression recognition using RAF-DB and AffectNet, while removing LaPa, WFLW, and AFLW2000 from the documented training/evaluation coverage. Appendix E.5 additionally states MORPH-II age training and evaluation, although the main dataset inventory omits it and no corresponding scores appear. FFHQ testing remains declared there despite removal of its result columns. Renamed visibility prediction still uses COFW landmark-visibility labels.

E2.justification: The comparison sets are substantially revised. v2 adds evaluated Faceptor comparisons for parsing, landmarks, age, expression, and attributes, and SwinFace/QFace comparisons for expression and attributes. HyperFace and AllinOne disappear from numerical comparisons. STAR Loss is removed from the 300W comparison but added for 300VW; 6DRepNet disappears from BIWI and ProS from CelebA. New specialist comparisons also accompany expression, age, and visibility evaluation.

E3.justification: Age evaluation changes from accuracy to MAE, and visibility from accuracy to recall at 80% precision. The 300VW aggregate becomes category-specific reporting, while the LFWA result changes from attribute accuracy to explicitly labeled gender accuracy. v2 reports three additional training epochs for unspecified tasks, revises augmentation settings, and changes task membership in backbone performance aggregates. Appendix C introduces new component-removal controls. These changes prevent treating revised scores as a controlled comparison between versions.

E4.justification: v1's segmentation/regression/classification task-synergy ablation is removed. v2 adds experiments testing removal of multi-scale features and the FaceX decoder in Table C.1. Backbone analysis adds MobileNet but removes several size variants and task-specific efficiency comparisons; WFLW condition-specific analyses also disappear. Appendix D adds qualitative examples exposing age/race inconsistencies. The racial-group bias analysis is retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without experimental seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. Category-specific scores in v2 do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Reported FaceXFormer results change substantially: CelebAMask-HQ F1 changes from 89.83 to 92.01, 300W full-set NME from 3.52 in v1 Table 10 to 3.05 in v2 Table 4, BIWI MAE from 3.65 to 3.52, and CelebA accuracy from 91.79 to 91.83. These accompany changed methods and training settings. v2 adds RAF-DB accuracy of 88.24 and replaces age/visibility results under different metrics. Retained baseline values also change, including AGRNet's parsing mean from 90.67 to 89.91. FFHQ scores and standalone race accuracies disappear; headline throughput changes from 37 to 33.21 FPS.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of the joint objective changes from v1 Equation 5 to v2 Section 3.4, separating age from gender/race and adding expression supervision. Fusion and attention equations remain substantively unchanged. Neither version provides formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The claimed unified capability expands from eight to nine tasks. The contribution narrative shifts from task synergy and competitive heterogeneous-task performance toward state-of-the-art performance across multiple tasks, including landmarks and head pose, where v1 explicitly acknowledged shortcomings. Real-time operation remains a core claim, with revised reported throughput.

C2.justification: v1 explains regression shortcomings through task interference and avoidance of heatmaps and advanced pose representations. v2 removes that account and adds interpretations of the decoder and multi-scale ablations. Its limitations newly emphasize complete retraining when adding tasks, and Appendix D acknowledges age/race prediction inconsistencies. Lack of interactivity remains, while future work shifts toward large pretrained models with zero-shot capabilities.

D1.justification: Reported hardware changes from eight 24GB A5000 GPUs to eight 48GB A6000 GPUs. v2 adds expression-specific augmentation instructions and MORPH-II dataset details, removes earlier parsing-specific augmentation probabilities, and changes the project-page link target. Most optimizer, batch-size, learning-rate, and sampling details remain. The extra training epochs are incompletely specified because the affected tasks are unnamed.

R1.justification: v1 positions HyperFace and AllinOne as the principal multi-task predecessors. v2 substantially revises this positioning by discussing SwinFace, QFace, and Faceptor as transformer/token-based peers and emphasizing broader task coverage. It removes the selective-search critique of earlier models and substantially expands citations supporting expression, age, visibility, and other specialist comparisons.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, results narrative, and limitations are extensively rewritten. Ablation studies become a separate main section, bias analysis moves out of Discussions, and appendix organization changes substantially as detailed benchmark material moves into the main results. These are substantial narrative and structural revisions beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: The main text switches from single-column to two-column layout. The broad benchmark table is reorganized into task-specific comparisons, incorporating revised appendix tables, expanded columns, and colored rankings. The task overview is redesigned. v1 Figure 5 becomes v2 Figure 3; the earlier token-query and baseline-comparison figures disappear, while Figure D.1 adds new examples. Efficiency and ablation displays are also substantially reorganized.

improvement.justification: v2 adds useful component ablations and contemporary multi-task comparisons, but removes task-synergy evidence and several strong baselines while broadening superiority claims. Reporting problems complicate the gains: v2 Table 2 reports 92.01 although its displayed class scores average 91.01; v1's analogous discrepancy was smaller, 89.83 versus 89.73. Table C.1 also mislabels head-pose and landmark metrics. These evidence gains and reliability losses prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
